title: Delta Lake Partitioning Strategy
summary: Decide whether to partition a Delta table, when liquid clustering or compaction is better, how Direct Lake, the SQL endpoint and Warehouse consume the layout, and how to implement and operate it.
audience: Data engineers, architects, platform and capacity owners

pages.title: Overview
pages.description: What the partitioning decision covers, the default answer, and a decision tree for the exceptions.

pages.title: Why and when to partition
pages.description: Partition pruning, small-file arithmetic, concurrent-writer isolation, cardinality limits and the principles behind the defaults.

pages.title: Fabric layout features
pages.description: V-Order, optimize write, auto compaction, adaptive file size, OPTIMIZE, Z-Order, VACUUM and liquid clustering, and how they combine.

pages.title: Patterns by layer and consumer
pages.description: Bronze, Silver and Gold layouts, Direct Lake, SQL analytics endpoint and Warehouse considerations, and neutral worked examples.

pages.title: Implementation examples
pages.description: Create partitioned and clustered tables, append, replace a slice, run concurrent merges, and change a layout safely.

pages.title: Validation and operations
pages.description: Measure layout health, diagnose small files, keep the SQL endpoint in sync, schedule maintenance and use the checklist.
